note: Attacker-controlled input bytes are split into 75-byte null-terminated argv strings; one string is the '-Y' option and the next is its optarg config line.
The '-Y' option passes its optarg (the attacker-controlled config line) to netsnmp_config_remember, which strdup's it into the memory list.
The config line is stored as a heap-allocated string in the read_config_memory list for later processing.
init_snmp (called from snmp_parse_args) invokes read_premib_configs, which processes all remembered config lines.
Processes the remembered config lines with when=PREMIB_CONFIG.
Each remembered line is passed to snmp_config_when; the attacker line 'abc' is a single token with no trailing delimiter.
buf is a copy of the line; strtok_r returns the whole line 'abc' as the only token since there are no delimiters.
start_from = line + 0 + 3 + 1 = line+4, which is one byte past the null terminator at line+3 because the token extends to the end of the line.
skip_white reads the byte at line+4, one past the heap allocation's null terminator, causing a heap-buffer-overflow READ 1.
